correctness.rationale: Concavity of lambda2 on mean-zero subspace and edge-orbit averaging reduce a global independent-weight optimum to two class rates. Core/leaf Laplacian decomposes into blocks with eigenvalues μ±(a η,b); μ-(a lambda,b) is gap and its target t condition is b>t,a lambda>=t(2b-t)/(b-t). Minimization of c(2+1/(u-1))+Qu for u=b/t>1 yields unique u=1+sqrt(c/Q), hence exact D and rates. For a cyclic core both cosine/sine Fiedler vectors saturate their Rayleigh quotients at any optimum; private-leaf equations force all b_i common, complex rim equation imaginary part forces all a_i common. Direct 52 finite weighted Laplacian cases corroborate, not replace, proof.

Existing weighted corona spectra provide eigenvalues, not optimization or all-nonuniform rigidity.

value.rationale: Closed all-core-class benchmark for spectral mixing under meaningful edge costs, with nontrivial global uniqueness for cycles and three distinct large-size scales. This answers design tradeoffs beyond routine substitution in spectral formula.

final_claim: For connected vertex-/edge-transitive d-regular core H with m vertices and first positive Laplacian eigenvalue lambda, independent nonnegative core/leaf rates under prices P,Q budget B attain max lambda2=B/[m(2c+Q+2sqrt(cQ))], c=dP/(2lambda). A two-rate optimum is explicit; when H is a cycle it is the unique global optimizer even without symmetry, with distinct n^-1, n^-2, n^-3 rates/gap asymptotics.
